description: Given a 2D array intervals where intervals[i] = [left_i, right_i] and an array queries, for each query return the size of the smallest interval containing it, or -1 if no interval contains it.
intuition: Process queries offline by sorting them alongside intervals. A min-heap keyed by interval size lets you always access the smallest covering interval, while lazy deletion removes intervals that no longer cover the current query point.
approach: Sort intervals by left endpoint and queries by value. Use a min-heap keyed by interval size. For each query, add all intervals whose left <= query, remove those whose right < query, and return the top of the heap.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: intervals = [[1,4],[2,4],[3,6],[4,4]], queries = [2,3,4,5]
sortedQ = [[0,2],[1,3],[2,4],[3,5]]
q=2 (qi=0): add intervals with left<=2: [1,4](size=4), [2,4](size=3). pq=[(3,4),(4,4)]
  pq.front=[3,4], right=4>=2 -> result[0]=3
q=3 (qi=1): add intervals with left<=3: [3,6](size=4). pq=[(3,4),(4,4),(4,6)]
  pq.front=[3,4], right=4>=3 -> result[1]=3
q=4 (qi=2): add [4,4](size=1). pq=[(1,4),(3,4),(4,4),(4,6)]
  pq.front=[1,4], right=4>=4 -> result[2]=1
q=5 (qi=3): no new intervals. pq.front=[1,4] but right=4<5 -> remove. Next=(3,4) right=4<5 -> remove...
  pq.front=[4,6], right=6>=5 -> result[3]=4
Return [3,3,1,4]
explanation:
1. Sort intervals by left endpoint. Sort queries by value (keeping original indices).
2. For each query, push all intervals with left <= query onto a min-heap (keyed by size).
3. Remove intervals from the heap whose right endpoint < query (no longer valid).
4. The top of the heap is the smallest interval containing the query.
5. Store the result at the original query index.
timeComplexity: O(n log n + q log q)
hints: Sort both intervals and queries to process them together.
Use a min-heap to track the smallest interval covering the current query.
Lazily remove expired intervals from the heap.

phases.label: Pair queries with indices and sort them
Insert each interval at most once
Remove each expired heap entry at most once

simplifications: O(3n log n + q log q + 2q)
O(n log n + q log q)
timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Both while loops share forward progress across all queries. Queries themselves only read the heap root. Sorting q queries cannot be omitted or expressed using log n when q can grow independently.
